Lessons.Title: Analyzing Graphs
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: determine exponential growth versus decay from graphs and descriptions; infer factors and starting values; compare two exponential decays on common graph scales and explain when their relative size changes. Original Edulytiks lesson aligned with Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 5 Lesson 6, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/5/6/preparation.html and student tasks https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/5/6/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source compares phone depreciation; our independent data are purely hypothetical.

Original fictional devices A and B have first-year price models in dollars A(t)=600(0.6)^t and B(t)=400(0.8)^t, t≥0 whole years. At t0 A600>B400, at t1 A360>B320, while at t2 A216<B256. Thus A first becomes lower than B at the second whole-year observation even though it began more expensive. A retains60% per year, B80%, so A loses40% annually compared with B's20%.

From a graph and table, the t0 vertical intercept reveals initial value, while the ratio of same-interval outputs reveals the multiplier. A greater initial value does not imply slower decay; compare both intercept and factor. If graph windows use different y scales, direct visual comparison may be misleading.

Student task: draw both on shared dollar/time axes with all four points t0–3; infer equations by common ratios, classify which decays faster and find the first integer observation where order reverses. Teacher-scored rubric (0–2 each, max8): correct plotted data, inferred parameters, accurate graph comparison, and evidence-backed contextual claims.

KeyConcepts.Title: Initial value from intercept
KeyConcepts.Definition: At input t0, output equals the exponential coefficient a.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Read at the same graph input.

KeyConcepts.Title: Decay factor from ratios
KeyConcepts.Definition: For each whole-step increase, output ratio is b.

KeyConcepts.Title: Relative decay comparison
KeyConcepts.Definition: Order can reverse because a smaller multiplier reduces one curve faster.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Compare actual paired values at same times.

WorkedExamples.Method: Investigate the first-party growth/decay table and independently check differences, ratios, exponents, and context.

WorkedExamples.Title: Determine first integer year below
WorkedExamples.Question: When is A(t) less than B(t) at an integer sampled year?
WorkedExamples.Method: Investigate the first-party growth/decay table and independently check differences, ratios, exponents, and context.
Steps: Therefore the first nonnegative integer year with A below B is t2.
This conclusion uses integer-year values rather than claiming exact continuous crossing time.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Year2 is first sampled year A<B.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Different scale may make one decay look faster.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use common axes or compute factors.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming higher initial output means higher forever

SummaryPoints: Exponential graph start and ratios determine its model.
Two decay curves can cross as retention factors differ.
A first falls below B at whole year2 in the original model.
Teacher evaluates graph reasoning and limits.
